Welcher? e Was für ein?, passo a passo: Welcher? and Was für ein?, step by step
PASSO 1: «welcher, welche, welches» sign: STEP 1: «welcher, welche, welches» means "WHICH" and picks from known options: «Welcher Pullover gefällt dir?» (Which sweater do you like?). STEP 2: it declines like «der, die, das» and like «dieser»: nominative: welcher Mann, welche Frau, welches Kind, welche Kinder; accusative: welchen Mann, welche Frau, welches Kind, welche Kinder; dative: welchem Mann, welcher Frau, welchem Kind, welchen Kindern. STEP 3: an adjective after it takes the endings it would take after the definite article: «Welchen blauen Pullover?» STEP 4: «was für ein» means "WHAT KIND OF": «Was für ein Film ist das?» (What kind of movie is it?). Here «ein» declines like the indefinite article and «was für» stays fixed: «Was für einen Film möchtest du sehen?» (masculine accusative). STEP 5: for the plural, no article: «Was für Filme magst du?» (What kind of movies do you like?)
o português usa «qual» para escolher («q: English makes the same distinction: "which" (choosing from options) vs "what kind of" (the category). German: «welcher» (which) vs «was für ein» (what kind of). The difference is that «welcher» changes its ending like «der».

As quatro formas de «quem», passo a pass: The four forms of "who", step by step
PASSO 1: «quem?» muda com o CASO, como o: STEP 1: "who?" changes with the CASE, like the pronouns — English still has who / whom / whose: «wer» (nominative, subject): «Wer kommt?» (Who's coming?); «wen» (accusative, direct object): «Wen siehst du?» (Whom do you see?); «wem» (dative): «Wem hilfst du?» (Who are you helping? — to whom); «wessen» (genitive): «Wessen Auto ist das?» (Whose car is that?). STEP 2: with a PREPOSITION, the preposition comes first and decides the case — no dangling prepositions as in English "Who are you talking to?": «Mit wem sprichst du?» (mit + dative), «Für wen ist das?» (für + accusative), «Von wem ist der Brief?» (von + dative), «Zu wem gehst du?» (zu + dative). STEP 3: the answer uses the same case: «Mit wem sprichst du? — Mit meinem Chef.» STEP 4: remember the prepositions and the cases they take (lessons 28 and 29).

PASSO 1: «man» (a gente, se, uma pessoa: STEP 1: «man» (one, you, people in general) takes the «er» form of the verb: «Man darf hier nicht rauchen» (You can't smoke here). It's like English "one" or general "you" — and careful: «man» is not "man" (that's «der Mann»). STEP 2: «jemand» (someone) and «niemand» (no one) change in the accusative and dative: «jemanden», «niemanden»; «jemandem», «niemandem»: «Ich sehe niemanden» (I don't see anyone), «Ich helfe niemandem.» STEP 3: «etwas» (something), «nichts» (nothing), «alles» (everything) don't change: «Ich brauche etwas», «Er sagt nichts», «Sie weiß alles.» STEP 4: an adjective after them becomes a neuter noun, capitalized, with -es — like English "something new": «Hast du etwas Neues?» (Anything new?), «nichts Gutes» (nothing good). STEP 5: «alle» (all, everyone) and «viele» (many) are plural: «Alle Kinder spielen», «Viele Leute kommen.»
